subject: Streaming billing: incomplete generations & retry/disconnect charges
messages:

Cc: Alex Cho <alex.legal@acme.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on streaming charges for incomplete sessions

Marcus —

Quick one: our engineering team noticed a spike in charges last week for a series of streaming calls that disconnected mid-generation. The tokens billed on the invoice look like the full chunk, even though the client never received the final completion. Can you confirm how Redwood charges for streaming responses when the connection drops before the model finishes? Also, in two cases our client retried the request and ended up paying twice — is there a retry/grace policy?

I attached the invoice lines and a sample request trace (invoice stub). We need a short write-up for our procurement team so we can reconcile the billing before our payment run.

Thanks,
Jordan Fields
Procurement, Acme AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming charges for incomplete sessions

Jordan —

Thanks for flagging this and for the invoice excerpt. Short answer: streaming is billed for tokens the server has emitted (not for internal generation attempts that were never returned), but there are edge cases around network disconnects and client-side retries that can lead to double charges.

A few clarifications:
- If the server proactively emits tokens and the TCP/HTTP stream delivers them to the client, those tokens are billable even if the connection then closes.
- If the server never sent the final chunk (e.g., generator state lost before emit), there should be no charge for those missing tokens.
- Client retries: if a client resubmits a request and the model re-generates tokens, those will be billed separately. We do not automatically dedupe charges across distinct requests.

From your trace it looks like cases #2 and #3 occurred: the model emitted the final chunk but the client-side reconnect retry led to a second successful generation that was also billed. We can help reconcile with logs and, for customers on enterprise contracts, evaluate a one-time adjustment.

I attached our internal note on streaming billing rules for your review.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share the full request ids/timestamps for the affected rows so we can correlate logs.
2) If you want, we can propose a one-time credit to offset the duplicate retry charges while we discuss guardrails.
3) We can schedule a 30-min call to walk engineering through recommended client retry behaviour (idempotency keys, resume windows).

Warmly,
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-streaming-billing-guidelines.pdf (internal-note)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question on streaming charges for incomplete sessions

Looping in details from the enterprise desk — Jordan, quick context from our side:

- For enterprise customers on committed plans we often allow an operational credit for verified double-billing due to retries; amount is evaluated per-case.
- We don't currently have server-side automatic deduplication for identical near-simultaneous requests, but we recommend: idempotency token + a client-side resume window (e.g., 12s) to avoid duplicate full re-runs.
- For broader contract language we can add a clause that clarifies streaming interruption credits (example language below).

Suggested credit approach for reconciliation: one-time credit equal to the lesser of (a) duplicate billed token cost or (b) $1,000, whichever is smaller, for this invoice cycle. If Acme prefers a larger credit we can escalate to Sales Leadership and Legal.

I’ll draft proposed contract language if Jordan wants it in writing.

— Priyom
